newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma govt says Suu Kyi restrictions to stay.
newsitem.headline: Burma govt says Suu Kyi restrictions to stay.

text.p: Burma's military government will maintain restrictions on the movements of Nobel Peace laureate Aung San Suu Kyi after recent unrest for the democracy leader's own safety, a top official said on Thursday.

Senior intelligence official Colonel Thein Swe told Reuters the decision made in early December to require Suu Kyi to inform the government of her movements and visitors was made to protect, not inconvenience, her.

"We are concerned for her. We are responsible for her safety, and if something happens to her we have to take the blame," Thein Swe told Reuters after the State Law and Order Restoration Council's (SLORC) monthly news briefing.
He said he did not know when the restrictions might be lifted, saying only it would be when the situation normalised.
But Suu Kyi, who was released from six years of house arrest in July 1995, told Reuters in a telephone interview on Thursday it was "very silly" to presume the restrictions were made for her benefit.
"That's a very silly thing to say. I don't take them seriously and hope you don't either," she said. "I don't think they are helping me in any way."

SLORC officials in early December placed restrictions on Suu Kyi following a wave of student protests when several thousand students took to the street in rare demonstrations against the military authorities. The government has accused Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) party of being involved and politicising the student protests.
